A.name: Causal mechanism from provision to consequence
A.instruction: Score whether the comment traces a causal chain from the proposed provision to a consequence. 10 = it follows the provision through specific behavior or implementation steps to a safety, health, environmental, or administrative consequence, with each link stated. 0 = it asserts that harm or benefit will occur without naming any intervening step.
A.original_name: Causal mechanism from provision to consequence
A.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces a credible chain from the proposed provision through behavior or implementation to a safety, health, environmental, or administrative consequence; score 0 when it merely asserts that harm or benefit will occur.

A.name: Marks the limits of its evidence and reasons from them
A.instruction: Score whether the comment separates what it knows from what it does not, and whether its recommendation follows from that separation. 10 = it states where the evidence runs out, names the specific unknowns, and gives a recommendation responsive to that uncertainty, such as precaution, a specified disclosure, or a question it says must be resolved first. 5 = uncertainty is acknowledged in passing and changes nothing. 0 = uniform certainty regardless of basis, or hedging with no consequence attached.
A.original_name: Marks the limits of its evidence and reasons from them
A.original_instruction: Score whether the comment distinguishes what it knows from what it does not, and whether the recommendation follows from that distinction. 10 = the comment states where the evidence runs out, identifies the specific unknowns, and derives a recommendation that is responsive to the uncertainty (precaution, a specified disclosure, a question the agency must answer before proceeding). 5 = uncertainty is acknowledged in passing and does not affect the recommendation. 0 = uniform certainty regardless of basis, or hedging with no consequence attached.

A.name: Credible alternative meeting the regulatory objective
A.instruction: Score whether the comment offers a worked alternative to the proposal. 10 = it proposes a specific alternative, exception, phase-in, or substitute and explains why that option can achieve the same regulatory objective, naming the relevant tradeoffs. 0 = it only registers support for or opposition to the proposal as written.
A.original_name: Credible alternative meeting the regulatory objective
A.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment proposes a specific alternative, exception, phase-in, or substitute and explains why it can achieve the same objective with relevant tradeoffs; score 0 when it only supports or opposes the proposal.

A.name: Implementation realism
A.instruction: Score whether the comment addresses what carrying out the proposal would practically require. 10 = it maps specific steps, resources, timing, personnel, or supply-chain conditions needed to implement the proposal. 0 = it ignores implementation realities and treats the proposal as self-executing.
A.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment maps the practical steps, resources, timing, personnel, or supply-chain conditions needed to implement the proposal; score 0 when it ignores implementation realities.

A.name: Tradeoff and side-effect analysis
A.instruction: Score whether the comment weighs the proposal's benefits against what it costs. 10 = it sets benefits against costs, risks, displaced protections, or unintended effects and states what the resulting tradeoff is. 0 = it presents one-sided approval or one-sided opposition, with nothing on the other side of the ledger.
A.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment weighs the proposal’s benefits against costs, risks, displaced protections, or unintended effects and explains the relevant tradeoff; score 0 when it presents only one-sided approval or opposition.

A.name: Cross-rule and system interaction
A.instruction: Score whether the comment relates the proposal to another rule, program, document, or process. 10 = it identifies a specific overlap, contradiction, gap, or sequencing problem with that other instrument and specifies how to resolve it. 0 = it analyzes the proposal in isolation and refers to no other rule, program, document, or process.
A.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies overlap, contradiction, gap, or sequencing with another rule, program, document, or process and specifies how to resolve it; score 0 when it analyzes the proposal in isolation.

A.name: Quantified supporting evidence
A.instruction: Score whether the comment supports its position with numbers. 10 = it uses relevant numerical data, calculations, comparisons, or rates that bear on its position and are stated concretely enough to be checked. 0 = it offers no verifiable quantitative support at all.
A.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses relevant numerical data, calculations, comparisons, or rates to support its position; score 0 when it provides no verifiable quantitative support.

A.name: Distributional consequence analysis
A.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies who bears distinct effects from the proposal. 10 = it names particular vulnerable, dependent, underserved, or differently situated groups and explains the mechanism by which those groups are affected differently. 0 = it invokes the broad public interest without identifying any affected group.
A.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies which vulnerable, dependent, underserved, or differently situated groups bear distinct effects and explains the mechanism; score 0 when it invokes broad public interest without identifying affected groups.

A.name: Ask serves more than the commenter's own burden or exposure
A.instruction: Score who benefits from the change the comment requests, as the comment itself frames it. 10 = the change would improve the rule's functioning for third parties, the protected resource, or the public, including where it plainly costs the commenter something. 5 = the ask helps the commenter, but the stated reasons are about workability for everyone. 0 = the ask is entirely relief for the submitter (delay, exemption, a higher threshold, more time), and its public-interest framing adds no independent content.
A.original_name: Ask serves more than the commenter's own burden or exposure
A.original_instruction: Score the beneficiary of the requested change as the comment itself frames it. 10 = the change would improve the rule's functioning for third parties, the protected resource, or the public, including where it plainly costs the commenter something. 5 = mixed: the ask helps the commenter but the stated reasons are about workability for everyone. 0 = the entire ask is relief for the submitter -- delay, exemption, a higher threshold, more time -- with the public-interest framing supplying no independent content.

A.name: Explicit evidence-to-requested-remedy linkage
A.instruction: Score whether the comment draws an explicit, traceable line from the evidence or reasoning it presents to the exact provision, number, or action it asks be changed. 10 = the requested remedy is derived step by step from the stated evidence, so the derivation can be followed. 0 = evidence or complaint and a specific ask sit as disconnected pieces, with no traceable link between them.
A.original_instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment draws an explicit, traceable line from the evidence or reasoning it presents to the exact provision, number, or action it asks the agency to change. A 10 shows the requested remedy derived transparently, step by step, from the stated evidence. A 0 presents evidence/complaint and a specific ask as disconnected pieces, with no traceable link between them.

A.name: Audits the agency's own figures, record, or arithmetic
A.instruction: Score whether the comment tests the agency's stated justification against numbers or statements the agency itself placed in the record. 10 = it reworks the agency's arithmetic, or sets the proposal against the agency's own admission or its own prior rule, and shows the figures so the check can be reproduced. 5 = it disputes a number but supplies no computation or source. 0 = the agency's figures are accepted or ignored, and the comment argues only from preference.
A.original_name: Audits the agency's own figures, record, or arithmetic
A.original_instruction: Score whether the comment tests the agency's stated justification against numbers or statements the agency itself placed in the record. 10 = the comment reworks the agency's arithmetic, or juxtaposes the proposal with the agency's own admission or its own prior rule, and shows the figures so the check is reproducible. 5 = the comment disputes a number but supplies no computation or source. 0 = the agency's figures are accepted or ignored entirely; the comment engages only at the level of preference.

A.name: Applies a controlling standard to the facts rather than citing it
A.instruction: Score whether the comment works the proposal's facts through a governing legal, scientific, or professional standard. 10 = the standard is named, its elements are identified, and the proposal's facts are matched against those elements to show fit or misfit, with that result driving the recommendation. 5 = a standard is invoked and a conclusion asserted, with the application left implicit. 0 = authority or the notice is quoted or summarized at length in place of analysis, or no standard is engaged.
A.original_name: Applies a controlling standard to the facts rather than citing it
A.original_instruction: Score whether the comment takes a governing legal, scientific, or professional standard and works the proposal's facts through it. 10 = the standard is named, its elements are identified, and the proposal's facts are matched against those elements to show fit or misfit, with the mismatch driving the recommendation. 5 = a standard is invoked and the conclusion asserted, with the application left implicit. 0 = authority or the notice is quoted or summarized at length in place of analysis, or no standard is engaged.

A.name: Surfaces an affected class or case the proposal overlooked
A.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a specific category of person, entity, or operating situation that the proposal's text does not appear to contemplate, or contemplates wrongly. 10 = a concrete class or edge case is named, its exclusion or misclassification is tied to specific proposal language, and the resulting harm or absurdity is stated. 5 = a gap is gestured at, but neither the class nor the consequence is made concrete. 0 = the comment discusses only the population the notice already addresses.
A.original_name: Surfaces an affected class or case the proposal overlooked
A.original_instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a specific category of person, entity, or operating situation that the proposal's text does not appear to contemplate, or contemplates wrongly, and shows the consequence of that gap. 10 = a concrete class or edge case is named, its exclusion or misclassification is tied to specific proposal language, and the resulting harm or absurdity is stated. 5 = a gap is gestured at but neither the class nor the consequence is made concrete. 0 = the comment discusses only the population the notice already addresses.

A.name: Identifies an internal inconsistency between parts of the proposal
A.instruction: Score whether the comment shows a specific conflict inside the proposal. 10 = it points to two parts of the proposed rule or its preamble that cannot both hold and says why they cannot. 0 = no inconsistency is identified, or a conflict is alleged without naming the two parts that clash.
A.original_name: Identifies an internal inconsistency between parts of the proposal
A.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment points to two parts of the proposed rule or its preamble that cannot both hold, and says why. Score 0 when no inconsistency is identified. Judge whether a specific conflict is shown.

A.name: States the conditions under which its own recommendation would fail
A.instruction: Score whether the comment states limits on its own recommendation. 10 = it names circumstances in which its own proposed course of action would not work, or the evidence that would change its recommendation. 0 = it offers no such limits on its own claim.
A.original_name: States the conditions under which its own recommendation would fail
A.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment names the circumstances in which its own proposed course of action would not work, or what evidence would change its recommendation. Score 0 when the comment offers no such limits. Judge whether limits on its own claim are stated.

B.name: Agency-relationship cues
B.instruction: Score whether the comment refers to a prior or ongoing relationship with the agency. 10 = it mentions prior meetings, ongoing collaboration, earlier submissions, established partnerships, or direct exchanges with agency personnel. 0 = it carries only a generic salutation and no relationship history. This is a surface feature: score the presence of the cues, not what they imply about the comment's worth.
B.upstream_parent: Existing relationships and insider access within the agency or docket lifecycle
B.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment mentions prior meetings, ongoing collaboration, earlier submissions, established partnerships, or direct exchanges with agency personnel; score 0 when it has only a generic salutation and no relationship history.

B.name: Credential and status parade
B.instruction: Score whether the comment's opening prominently parades the writer's status markers. 10 = the opening prominently lists multiple degrees, certifications, fellowships, offices, titles, or years of experience. 0 = no status or expertise signals appear. This is a surface feature: score the display of the markers, not the writer's actual expertise.
B.upstream_parent: Submitter's professional seniority, standing, and access to policymakers
B.original_instruction: Score 10 when the opening prominently lists multiple degrees, certifications, fellowships, offices, titles, or years of experience; score 0 when no status or expertise signals appear.

B.name: Professional document apparatus
B.instruction: Score whether the submission carries professional document-production apparatus. 10 = it contains elaborate exhibits, master indexes, slide decks, service-bulletin reproductions, revision histories, or attachment-heavy packaging. 0 = it is a plain standalone comment with no document-production signals. This is a surface feature: score the packaging, not the quality of what is packaged.
B.upstream_parent: Availability of lawyers, engineers, consultants, and professional document-production resources
B.original_instruction: Score 10 when the submission contains elaborate exhibits, master indexes, slide decks, service-bulletin reproductions, revision histories, or attachment-heavy packaging; score 0 for a plain standalone comment with no document-production signals.

B.name: First-person credential or stake self-disclosure
B.instruction: Score how explicitly and prominently the comment establishes the writer's own identity, credentials, professional role, or stake, as in 'I am a Professor...', 'I have X years of experience...', 'I represent...', or naming a degree, certification, or affiliation. 10 = the comment opens with or centers on an extended personal or professional credential or identity statement. 0 = no self-identifying credential or stake language appears at all. Score the disclosure itself, whether or not that identity is load-bearing for the argument.
B.upstream_parent: submitter's professional standing, expertise, or personal stake in the issue, and an instinct to lead with ethos-establishing credentials
B.original_instruction: Score how explicitly and prominently the comment establishes the writer's personal identity, credentials, professional role, or stake in the issue (e.g. 'I am a Professor...', 'I have X years of experience...', 'I represent...', naming a degree, certification, or affiliation) as a rhetorical move, independent of whether that identity is actually load-bearing for the argument's substance. 10 = the comment opens with or centers on an extended personal/professional credential or identity statement. 0 = the comment contains no self-identifying credential or stake language at all.

B.name: Emotional advocacy intensity
B.instruction: Score how intense the comment's emotional advocacy register is. 10 = repeated alarm, outrage, moral condemnation, emphatic praise, all-caps, exclamation marks, or vivid metaphors run through the text. 0 = the prose is consistently restrained and neutral. This is a surface feature: score the register, not whether the emotion is warranted.
B.original_instruction: Score 10 for repeated alarm, outrage, moral condemnation, emphatic praise, all-caps, exclamation marks, or vivid metaphors; score 0 for consistently restrained, neutral prose.

B.name: NGO action-alert templated phrasing
B.instruction: Score whether the comment uses stock activist phrasing typical of NGO mass-comment action-alert tools. 10 = it strongly exhibits that templated register: formulaic gratitude closings ('THANK YOU for your commitment to...'), superlative-modified positions ('I HIGHLY support...', 'I strongly urge...'), and emphatic capitalized keywords, especially in a short, largely interchangeable one-fact-plus-a-plea structure. 0 = no such stock phrasing appears. This is a surface feature: score the phrasing, not the sincerity behind it.
B.upstream_parent: comment was generated or guided by an NGO/advocacy-group mass-comment campaign tool (e.g. a pre-filled web action alert) that supplies stock phrasing for the submitter to personalize
B.original_instruction: Score the presence of stock activist/action-alert phrasing typical of NGO mass-comment campaign tools: formulaic gratitude closings ('THANK YOU for your commitment to...'), superlative-modified statements of position ('I HIGHLY support...', 'I strongly urge...'), and emphatic capitalized keywords, especially combined with a short, largely interchangeable one-fact-plus-a-plea structure. 10 = the comment strongly exhibits this templated activist register. 0 = the comment shows no such stock phrasing.

B.name: Embedded formal citation within personal-voice prose
B.instruction: Score whether a formal citation sits embedded inside otherwise personal, informal, first-person prose. 10 = the narrating voice is personal and informal yet carries one or more formal legal or scholarly citations (a full case citation, a parenthetical citation to a named organization, a footnoted source) that read as inserted by another hand, creating a clear register shift. 0 = no such embedded citation appears, or the comment is uniformly formal or uniformly informal with no citations at all.
B.upstream_parent: the comment received legal or research assistance (e.g. an attorney or claims law firm representing a claimant, or a teacher/librarian helping a student) that supplied one or more specific supporting citations without otherwise rewriting the submitter's voice
B.original_name: Embedded formal citation within personal-voice prose
B.original_instruction: Score whether the comment juxtaposes an otherwise personal, informal, first-person narrative voice with one or more embedded formal legal or scholarly citations (e.g. a full case citation, a parenthetical citation to a named organization, a footnoted source) that read as though inserted by someone other than the narrating voice. 10 = a clear formal citation is embedded within personal/informal prose, creating a register shift. 0 = no such embedded citation is present, or the whole comment is uniformly formal or uniformly informal with no citations at all.

B.name: Formal itemized technical/regulatory rebuttal structure
B.instruction: Score how far the comment is laid out as a formal point-by-point regulatory rebuttal. 10 = the whole comment is addressed to a named official or office and broken into discrete numbered or lettered items, each citing a specific rule paragraph, CFR subsection, AD or docket number, or service-bulletin reference, with little connective persuasive narrative between points. 0 = it is continuous persuasive prose with no addressee-directed itemized rule-section corrections.
B.upstream_parent: the submitter is a regulated entity's engineering/compliance staff responding to a routine Airworthiness Directive or product-specific technical requirement as an established business process, not an independent stakeholder building a persuasive case
B.original_instruction: Score the degree to which the comment is organized as a formal point-by-point regulatory rebuttal: addressed to a named official/office, broken into discrete numbered or lettered items, each citing a specific rule paragraph, CFR subsection, AD/docket number, or service-bulletin reference, with little connective persuasive narrative between points. 10 = the entire comment is such a structured technical-correction list (e.g. 'Comment No1... Page/Paragraph/Section... What is the FAA's proposed requirement...'). 0 = the comment is continuous persuasive prose with no addressee-directed itemized rule-section corrections.

B.name: Docket number or RIN quoted verbatim
B.instruction: Score whether a docket identifier or RIN appears verbatim in the comment. 10 = such an identifier string is present in the text. 0 = neither a docket number nor a RIN appears. Score only whether the identifier string is present, never whether the comment addresses the right rule.
B.original_name: Docket number or RIN quoted verbatim
B.original_instruction: Score 10 when a docket identifier or RIN appears verbatim in the comment. Score 0 when neither appears. Score only whether the identifier string is present, never whether the comment addresses the right rule.

B.name: Text is entirely upper case
B.instruction: Score whether the comment's text is written in capital letters. 10 = it is wholly or almost wholly in capitals. 0 = it uses ordinary sentence casing. Score only the letter casing.
B.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment is written wholly or almost wholly in capital letters. Score 0 when it uses ordinary sentence casing. Score only the letter casing.
